name: Deepstash
tagline: A mobile-first app for discovering, saving and resurfacing bite-sized ideas from books and articles.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The part people think they are paying for, a place to stash ideas with tags and a daily resurfacing feed, is a one-sitting build. The part they are actually paying for is the library: tens of thousands of hand-cut idea cards from books, podcasts and articles, plus the people who keep cutting them. An agent can give you an empty stash with a nice spaced-repetition loop, and then you are the content team, forever. Feeding it yourself means reading the source material anyway, which is the exact work Deepstash exists to compress. Build the stash if you already have a highlight habit; do not expect the discovery feed to appear.
coreLoopDIY: A local app that ingests article URLs and manual notes, splits them into tagged idea cards, and serves a daily shuffle of five cards to re-read.
requirements: Node and a local machine to run it on
An internet connection for URL fetching and article text extraction
Your own reading habit, since nothing seeds the library for you
whatYouLose: The curated corpus: thousands of pre-chopped ideas from books you have not read
Community curation, following people whose taste filters the firehose for you
A polished mobile app with offline reading, widgets and notifications
Streaks, stats and the mild social pressure that actually drives daily use
Topic collections and recommendations that surface things you did not search for
moatNotes: The idea cards are derived from copyrighted books and articles, which is both the moat and the legal tightrope. You cannot scrape your way to it and you would not want to host it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Deepstash sells pre-digested insight, not storage. The subscription buys access to a library someone else assembled and a feed that keeps handing you something worth reading on a four minute train ride, which is a content business dressed as a productivity app. A personal clone gets the saving and the resurfacing right in an afternoon and then sits there empty, because the hard part was never the database schema. Most people who build the clone end up using it as a highlight archive and still open Deepstash for discovery.
notes: The stash is a weekend toy; the library is not. The moat is a licensed, hand-curated corpus of book and article ideas plus the community that keeps producing it.
prompt:
Build a local personal idea stash called Stash. Stack: Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript, Tailwind, and SQLite via better-sqlite3. Single user, runs on localhost, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Data model (SQLite, migrations in a single init script):
- sources: id, title, author, url, kind (article | book | podcast | manual), created_at
- cards: id, source_id, text (the idea, max 400 chars), note (my own words, optional), tags (JSON array), created_at, last_shown_at, times_shown, starred

Features, all in scope:
1. Add by URL: paste a link, fetch it server-side, extract readable text with @mozilla/readability plus jsdom, store the source, then show the extracted paragraphs in a split view where I click or select text to turn passages into cards.
2. Add manually: a form for book or podcast ideas with title, author and the idea text.
3. Tagging: freeform tags with autocomplete from existing tags.
4. Daily shuffle: a home screen that serves five cards, weighted toward cards with the oldest last_shown_at and highest starred value. Buttons: keep, star, archive. Update last_shown_at and times_shown.
5. Browse and search: full-text search over card text and notes using SQLite FTS5, filterable by tag and source.
6. Export: a button that dumps everything to a single Markdown file grouped by source, and a JSON dump.

Explicitly out of scope: any recommendation engine, any pre-seeded content library, social features, mobile apps, push notifications, auth.

UI: dark, one column, large type, keyboard shortcuts (j/k to move, s to star, a to archive, n for new). Make the daily shuffle the default route.

Store the SQLite file at ./data/stash.db and gitignore it. Put any config in .env.local with a .env.example checked in. Include a README with setup, and seed the database with three example cards so the UI is not empty on first run.
